In that respect,\n   * it's closer to a resolver as might be found in apollo-server\n   * - is used before a network request\n   * - is used when reading the cache\n   *\n   * It can be used to map field arguments to [CacheKey]:\n   *\n   * ```\n   * {\n   *   user(id: \"1\"}) {\n   *     id\n   *     firstName\n   *     lastName\n   *   }\n   * }\n   * ```\n   *\n   * ```\n   * override fun resolveField(field: CompiledField, variables: Executable.Variables, parent: Map<String, Any?>, parentId: String): Any? {\n   *   val id = field.resolveArgument(\"id\", variables)?.toString()\n   *   if (id != null) {\n   *     return CacheKey(id)\n   *   }\n   *\n   *   return super.resolveField(field, variables, parent, parentId)\n   * }\n   * ```\n   *\n   * The simple example above isn't very representative as most of the times `@fieldPolicy` can express simple argument mappings in a more\n   * concise way but still demonstrates how [resolveField] works.\n   *\n   * [resolveField] can also be generalized to return any value:\n   *\n   * ```\n   * override fun resolveField(field: CompiledField, variables: Executable.Variables, parent: Map<String, Any?>, parentId: String): Any? {\n   *   if (field.name == \"name\") {\n   *     // Every \"name\" field will return \"JohnDoe\" now!\n   *     return \"JohnDoe\"\n   *   }\n   *\n   *   return super.resolveField(field, variables, parent, parentId)\n   * }\n   * ```\n   *\n   * See also @fieldPolicy\n   * See also [CacheKeyGenerator]\n   *\n   * @param field the field to resolve\n   * @param variables the variables of the current operation\n   * @param parent the parent object as a map. It can contain the same values as [Record]. Especially, nested objects will be represented\n   * by [CacheKey]\n   * @param parentId the id of the parent. Mainly used for debugging\n   *\n   * @return a value that can go in a [Record]. No type checking is done. It is the responsibility of implementations to return the correct\n   * type\n   */\n  fun resolveField(\n      field: CompiledField,\n      variables: Executable.Variables,\n      parent: Map<String, @JvmSuppressWildcards Any?>,\n      parentId: String,\n  ): Any?\n}\n\n/**\n * A cache resolver that uses the parent to resolve fields.\n */\nobject DefaultCacheResolver : CacheResolver {\n  /**\n   * @param parent a [Map] that represent the object containing this field. The map values can have the same types as the ones in  [Record]\n   */\n  override fun resolveField(\n      field: CompiledField,\n      variables: Executable.Variables,\n      parent: Map<String, @JvmSuppressWildcards Any?>,\n      parentId: String,\n  ): Any? {\n    val fieldKey = field.nameWithArguments(variables)\n    if (!parent.containsKey(fieldKey)) {\n      throw CacheMissException(parentId, fieldKey)\n    }\n\n    return parent[fieldKey]\n  }\n}\n\n\n/**\n * A cache resolver that uses the cache date as a receive date and expires after a fixed max age\n */\n@ApolloExperimental\nclass ReceiveDateCacheResolver(private val maxAge: Int) : CacheResolver {\n  /**\n   * @param parent a [Map] that represent the object containing this field. The map values can have the same types as the ones in  [Record]\n   */\n  override fun resolveField(\n      field: CompiledField,\n      variables: Executable.Variables,\n      parent: Map<String, @JvmSuppressWildcards Any?>,\n      parentId: String,\n  ): Any? {\n    val fieldKey = field.nameWithArguments(variables)\n    if (!parent.containsKey(fieldKey)) {\n      thr","middle":"ow CacheMissException(parentId, fieldKey)\n    }\n\n","suffix":"    if (parent is Record) {\n      val lastUpdated = parent.date?.get(fieldKey)\n      if (lastUpdated != null) {\n        val age = currentTimeMillis() / 1000 - lastUpdated\n        if (age > maxAge) {\n          throw CacheMissException(parentId, fieldKey, true)\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    return parent[fieldKey]\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * A cache resolver that uses the cache date as an expiration date and expires past it\n */\n@ApolloExperimental\nclass ExpireDateCacheResolver() : CacheResolver {\n  /**\n   * @param parent a [Map] that represent the object containing this field. The map values can have the same types as the ones in  [Record]\n   */\n  override fun resolveField(\n      field: CompiledField,\n      variables: Executable.Variables,\n      parent: Map<String, @JvmSuppressWildcards Any?>,\n      parentId: String,\n  ): Any? {\n    val fieldKey = field.nameWithArguments(variables)\n    if (!parent.containsKey(fieldKey)) {\n      throw CacheMissException(parentId, fieldKey)\n    }\n\n    if (parent is Record) {\n      val expires = parent.date?.get(fieldKey)\n      if (expires != null) {\n        if (currentTimeMillis() / 1000 - expires >= 0) {\n          throw CacheMissException(parentId, fieldKey, true)\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    return parent[fieldKey]\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * A [CacheResolver] that uses @fieldPolicy annotations to resolve fields and delegates to [DefaultCacheResolver] else\n */\nobject FieldPolicyCacheResolver : CacheResolver {\n  override fun resolveField(\n      field: CompiledField,\n      variables: Executable.Variables,\n      parent: Map<String, @JvmSuppressWildcards Any?>,\n      parentId: String,\n  ): Any? {\n    val keyArgsValues = field.argumentValues(variables) { it.definition.isKey }.values.map { it.toString() }\n\n    if (keyArgsValues.isNotEmpty()) {\n      return CacheKey(field.type.rawType().name, keyArgsValues)\n    }\n\n    return DefaultCacheResolver.resolveField(field, variables, parent, parentId)\n  }\n}\n\n\n","code-engine":{"type":"TOKEN_MIDDLE","language":"Kotlin","ce-version":"0.3.119"}}

Flushing here makes them available to the reader\n        // as soon as they're available.\n        httpDataSink.flush()\n      }\n\n      override fun onComplete(error: NSError?) {\n        httpDataSink.close()\n        // This can be called with an error before `onResponse` if there's an error like no connectivity.\n        // It if it called *after* `onResponse`, do not resume the continuation again.\n        if (error != null && !hasDispatchedHttpResponse) continuation.resumeWith(\n            buildHttpResponse(\n                data = httpDataSource,\n                httpResponse = null,\n                error = error,\n            )\n        )\n      }\n    }\n\n    val task = nsUrlSession.dataTaskWithRequest(nsMutableURLRequest)\n    delegate.registerHandlerForTask(task, handler)\n\n    continuation.invokeOnCancellation {\n      task.cancel()\n    }\n    task.resume()\n  }\n\n  override fun close() {\n    nsUrlSession.invalidateAndCancel()\n  }\n}\n\nprivate fun buildHttpResponse(\n    data: BufferedSource,\n    httpResponse: NSHTTPURLResponse?,\n    error: NSError?,\n): Result<HttpResponse> {\n\n  if (error != null) {\n    return Result.failure(\n        ApolloNetworkException(\n            message = \"Failed to execute GraphQL http network request\",\n            platformCause = error\n        )\n    )\n  }\n\n  if (httpResponse == null) {\n    return Result.failure(\n        ApolloNetworkException(\"Failed to parse GraphQL http network response: EOF\")\n    )\n  }\n\n  val httpHeaders = httpResponse.allHeaderFields\n      .map { (key, value) ->\n        HttpHeader(key.toString(), value.toString())\n      }\n\n  val statusCode = httpResponse.statusCode.toInt()\n\n  return Result.success(\n      HttpResponse.Builder(statusCode = statusCode)\n          .headers(httpHeaders)\n          .body(bodySource = data)\n          .build()\n  )\n}\n\n/**\n * Order of the callbacks in the no-error case:\n * - didReceiveResponse\n * - didReceiveData\n * - didReceiveData\n * ...\n * - willCacheResponse\n *\n * Error case (e.g. no connectivity):\n * - didCompleteWithError (with a non-null error)\n */\nprivate class StreamingDataDelegate : NSObject(), NSURLSessionDataDelegateProtocol {\n  interface Handler {\n    fun onResponse(response: NSHTTPURLResponse)\n    fun onData(data: NSData)\n    fun onComplete(error: NSError?)\n  }\n\n  private val handlers = mutableMapOf<NSURLSessionTask, Handler>()\n\n  override fun URLSession(\n      session: NSURLSession,\n      dataTask: NSURLSessionDataTask,\n      didReceiveResponse: NSURLResponse,\n      completionHandler: (NSURLSessionResponseDisposition) -> Unit,\n  ) {\n    handlers[dataTask]?.onResponse(didReceiveResponse as NSHTTPURLResponse)\n    completionHandler(NSURLSessionResponseAllow)\n  }\n\n  override fun URLSession(\n      session: NSURLSession,\n      dataTask: NSURLSessionDataTask,\n      didReceiveData: NSData,\n  ) {\n    handlers[dataTask]?.onData(didReceiveData)\n  }\n\n  override fun URLSession(\n      session: NSURLSession,\n      task: NSURLSessionTask,\n      didCompleteWithError: NSError?,\n  ) {\n    handlers[task]?.onComplete(didCompleteWithError)\n\n    // Cleanup\n    handlers.remove(task)\n  }\n\n  override fun URLSession(\n      session: NSURLSession,\n      dataTask: NSURLSessionDataTask,\n      willCacheResponse: NSCachedURLResponse,\n      completionHandler: (NSCachedURLResponse?) -> Unit,\n  ) {\n    handlers[dataTask]?.onComplete(null)\n\n    // Cleanup\n    handlers.remove(dataTask)\n\n    completionHandler(willCacheResponse)\n  }\n\n  fun registerHandlerForTask(task: NSURLSessionTask, handler: Handler) {\n    handlers[task] = handler\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * A source and a sink that are attached. The sink's output is the source's input.\n * A [Buffer] is used internally to store the data.\n * A `pthread` `mutex` and `cond` are used to block the source's reading until there is data to read, or the sink is closed. These are\n * released when both the sink and the source are closed.\n *\n * Inspired by okio's Pipe which is JVM only.\n */\nprivate class Pipe {\n  private val buffer = Buffer()\n\n  private val mutex = nativeHeap.alloc<pthread_mutex_t>()\n  private val cond = nativeHeap.alloc<pthread_cond_t>()\n\n  private var isSinkClosed = false\n  private var isSourceClosed = false\n\n  init {\n    pthread_mutex_init(mutex.ptr, null)\n    pthread_cond_init(cond.ptr, null)\n  }\n\n  val sink: Sink = object : Sink {\n    override fun write(source: Buffer, byteCount: Long) {\n      pthread_mutex_lock(mutex.ptr)\n      buffer.write(source, byteCount)\n      pthread_cond_broadcast(cond.ptr)\n      pthread_mutex_unlock(mutex.ptr)\n    }\n\n    override fun close() {\n      pthread_mutex_lock(mutex.ptr)\n      isSinkClosed = true\n      pthread_cond_broadcast(cond.ptr)\n      pthread_mutex_unlock(mutex.ptr)\n\n      disposeIfClosed()\n    }\n\n    override fun flush() {}\n    override fun timeout() = Timeout.NONE\n  }\n\n  val source: Source = object : Source {\n    override fun read(sink: Buffer, byteCount: Long): Long {\n      pthread_mutex_lock(mutex.ptr)\n      while (buffer.size == 0L && !isSinkClosed) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(cond.ptr, mutex.ptr)\n      }\n      val readCount = buffer.read(sink, byteCount)\n      pthread_mutex_unlock(mutex.ptr)\n      return readCount\n    }\n\n    override fun close() {\n      isSourceClosed = true\n      disposeIfClosed()\n    }\n\n    override fun timeout() = Timeout.NONE\n  }\n\n  private fun disposeIfClosed() {\n    if (isSourceClosed && isSinkClosed) {\n      pthread_mutex_destroy(mutex.ptr)\n      pthread_cond_destroy(cond.ptr)\n    }\n  }\n}\n","code-engine":{"type":"TOKEN_MIDDLE","language":"Kotlin","ce-version":"0.3.119"}}

This directory must be exclusive\n * to the cache; the cache may delete or overwrite files from its directory. It is an error for\n * multiple processes to use the same cache directory at the same time.\n *\n *\n * This cache limits the number of bytes that it will store on the filesystem. When the number of\n * stored bytes exceeds the limit, the cache will remove entries in the background until the limit\n * is satisfied. The limit is not strict: the cache may temporarily exceed it while waiting for\n * files to be deleted. The limit does not include filesystem overhead or the cache journal so\n * space-sensitive applications should set a conservative limit.\n *\n *\n * Clients call [.edit] to create or update the values of an entry. An entry may have only\n * one editor at one time; if a value is not available to be edited then [.edit] will return\n * null.\n *\n *\n *  * When an entry is being **created** it is necessary to supply a full set of\n * values; the empty value should be used as a placeholder if necessary.\n *  * When an entry is being **edited**, it is not necessary to supply data for\n * every value; values default to their previous value.\n *\n *\n *\n * Every [.edit] call must be matched by a call to [Editor.commit] or [ ][Editor.abort]. Committing is atomic: a read observes the full set of values as they were before\n * or after the commit, but never a mix of values.\n *\n *\n * Clients call [.get] to read a snapshot of an entry. The read will observe the value at\n * the time that [.get] was called. Updates and removals after the call do not impact ongoing\n * reads.\n *\n *\n * This class is tolerant of some I/O errors. If files are missing from the filesystem, the\n * corresponding entries will be dropped from the cache. If an error occurs while writing a cache\n * value, the edit will fail silently. Callers should handle other problems by catching `IOException` and responding appropriately.\n *\n *\n * Copied from OkHttp 3.14.2: https://github.com/square/okhttp/blob/\n * b8b6ee831c65208940c741f8e091ff02425566d5/\n * okhttp/src/main/java/okhttp3/internal/cache/DiskLruCache.java\n */\n\ninternal class DiskLruCache(\n/*\n     * This cache uses a journal file named \"journal\". A temporary file named\n     * \"journal.tmp\" will be used during compaction; that file should be deleted if\n     * it exists when the cache is opened.\n     */\n    private val fileSystem: FileSystem,\n    /** Returns the directory where this cache stores its data.  */\n    private val directory: File,\n    private val appVersion: Int, valueCount: Int, maxSize: Long,\n    executor: Executor,\n) : Closeable, Flushable {\n  private val journalFile: File = File(directory, JOURNAL_FILE)\n  private val journalFileTmp: File\n  private val journalFileBackup: File\n  private var maxSize: Long\n  val valueCount: Int\n  private var size: Long = 0\n  var journalWriter: BufferedSink? = null\n  val lruEntries = LinkedHashMap<String, Entry?>(0, 0.75f, true)\n  var redundantOpCount = 0\n  var hasJournalErrors = false\n\n  // Must be read and written when synchronized on 'this'.\n  var initialized = false\n\n  /** Returns true if this cache has been closed.  */\n  @get:Synchronized\n  var isClosed = false\n  var mostRecentTrimFailed = false\n  var mostRecentRebuildFailed = false\n\n  /**\n   * To differentiate between old and current snapshots, each entry is given a sequence number each\n   * time an edit is committed. }\n    }\n    rebuildJournal()\n    initialized = true\n  }\n\n  @Throws(IOException::class)\n  private fun readJournal() {\n    fileSystem.source(journalFile).buffer().use { source ->\n      val source.readUtf8LineStrict()\n      val blank = source.readUtf8LineStrict()\n      if (MAGIC != magic\n          || VERSION_1 != version\n          || appVersion.toString() != appVersionString\n valueCountString + \", \" + blank + \"]\")\n      }\n      var lineCount = 0\n      while (true) {\n        try {\n          readJournalLine(source.readUtf8LineStrict())\n          lineCount++\n @Throws(FileNotFoundException::class)\n  private fun newJournalWriter(): BufferedSink {\n    val fileSink = fileSystem.appendingSink(journalFile)\n    val faultHidingSink: Sink = object : line.substring(keyBegin, secondSpace)\n    }\n    var entry = lruEntries[key]\n    if (entry == null) {\n      entry = Entry(key)\n      lruEntries[key] = entry\n    }\n    if (secondSpace != -1 && firstSpace == CLEAN.length && line.startsWith(CLEAN)) {\n      val parts = line.substring(secondSpace + 1).split(\" \").toTypedArray()\n      entry.readable = true\n      entry.currentEditor = null\n firstSpace == READ.length && line.startsWith(READ)) {\n      // This work was already done by calling lruEntries.get().\n    } else {\n      throw IOException(\"unexpected journal line: $line\")\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Computes the initial size and collects garbage as a part of opening the cache. If the trim job failed, it means we are storing more data than\n      // requested by the user. Do not allow edits so we do not go over that limit any further. If\n      // the journal rebuild failed, the journal writer will not be active, meaning we will not be\n      // able to record the edit, causing file leaks. This iterator doesn't throw `ConcurrentModificationException`, but if new entries are added while iterating, those new\n   * entries will not be returned by the iterator. If existing entries are removed during iteration,\n   * they will be absent (unless they were already returned).\n   *\n   *\n   * If there are I/O problems during iteration, this iterator fails silently. Note that once\n     * an editor has been detached it is possible for another editor to edit the entry.\n     */\n    fun detach() {\n      if (entry.currentEditor == this) {\n        for (i in 0 until valueCount) {\n          try {\n            fileSystem.delete(entry.dirtyFiles[i])\n          } catch (e: IOException) {\n            // This file is potentially leaked. This releases the edit lock so another edit may be started on the same\n     * key.\n     */\n    @Throws(IOException::class)\n    fun abort() {\n      synchronized(this@DiskLruCache) {\n        check(!done)\n        if (entry.currentEditor == this) {\n          completeEdit(this, false)\n        }\n        done = true\n      }\n    }\n\n    fun abortUnlessCommitted() {\n      synchronized(this@DiskLruCache) {\n        if (!done && entry.currentEditor == this) {\n          try {\n            completeEdit(this, false)\n          } catch (ignored: IOException) {\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  inner class Entry internal constructor(val key: String) {\n    /** Lengths of this entry's files.  */\n    val lengths: LongArray = LongArray(valueCount)\n    val cleanFiles: Array<File>\n    val dirtyFiles: Array<File>\n\n    /** True if this entry has ever been published.  */\n    var readable = false\n\n    /** The ongoing edit or null if this entry is not being edited.  */\n    var currentEditor: Editor? This opens all streams eagerly to guarantee that we see a\n     * single published snapshot. If we opened streams lazily then the streams could come from\n     * different edits.\n     */\n    fun snapshot(): Snapshot? {\n      if (!Thread.holdsLock(this@DiskLruCache)) throw AssertionError()\n      val sources = arrayOfNulls<Source>(valueCount)\n      val lengths = lengths.clone() // Defensive copy since these can be zeroed out.\n      return try {\n        for (i in 0 until valueCount) {\n          sources[i] = fileSystem.source(cleanFiles[i])\n        }\n        @Suppress(\"UNCHECKED_CAST\")\n        Snapshot(key, sequenceNumber, sources as Array<Source>, lengths)\n      } catch (e: FileNotFoundException) {\n        // A file must have been deleted manually!\n        var i = 0\n        while (i < valueCount) {\n          if (sources[i] != null) {\n            closeQuietly(sources[i], \"file\")\n          } else {\n            break\n          }\n          i++\n        }\n        // Since the entry is no longer valid, remove it so the metadata is accurate (i.e. the cache\n        // size.)\n        try {\n          removeEntry(this)\n        } catch (ignored: IOException) {\n        }\n        null\n      }\n    }\n\n    init {\n      val tmpCleanFiles = mutableListOf<File>()\n      val tmpDirtyFiles = mutableListOf<File>()\n\n      // The names are repetitive so re-use the same builder to avoid allocations.\n      val fileBuilder = StringBuilder(key).append('.')\n      val truncateTo = fileBuilder.length\n      for (i in 0 until valueCount) {\n        fileBuilder.append(i)\n        tmpCleanFiles.add(File(directory, based on usage of [LinkedHashMap] as a container for the cache and custom\n * double linked queue to track LRU property.\n *\n * [maxSize] - maximum size of the cache, can be anything bytes, number of entries etc. By default is number o entries.\n * [weigher] - to be called to calculate the estimated size (weight) of the cache entry defined by its [Key] and [Value].\n *             By default it returns 1.\n *\n * Cache trim performed only on new entry ","middle":"insertion.\n */\ninternal class LruCache<Key, Value>(\n    private val maxSize: Int,\n    private val weigher: Weigher<Key, Value> = { _, _ -> 1 },\n) {\n  private val cache = LinkedHashMap<Key, Node<Key, Value>>(0, 0.75f)\n  private var headNode: Node<Key, Value>? = null\n  private var tailNode: Node<Key, Value>? = null\n  private var size: Int = 0\n\n  operator fun get(key: Key): Value? {\n    val node = cache[key]\n    if (node != null) {\n      moveNodeToHead(node)\n    }\n    return node?.value\n  }\n\n  operator }\n\n    trim()\n  }\n\n  fun remove(key: Key): Value? {\n    return removeUnsafe(key)\n  }\n\n  fun keys() = cache.keys\n\n  private fun removeUnsafe(key: Key): Value? {\n    val nodeToRemove = cache.remove(key)\n    val value = nodeToRemove?.value\n    if (nodeToRemove != null) {\n      unlinkNode(nodeToRemove)\n    }\n    return value\n  }\n\n  fun remove(keys: Collection<Key>) {\n    keys.forEach { key -> removeUnsafe(key) }\n  }\n\n  fun clear() {\n    cache.clear()\n    headNode = null\n    tailNode = null\n    size = 0\n  }\n\n  fun size(): Int {\n    return size\n  }\n\n  fun tailNode\n    while (nodeToRemove != null && size > maxSize) {\n      cache.remove(nodeToRemove.key)\n      unlinkNode(nodeToRemove)\n      nodeToRemove = tailNode\n    }\n  }\n\n  private fun {\n      node.next?.prev = node.prev\n    }\n\n    node.next = headNode\n    node.prev = null\n\n    headNode?.prev = node\n    headNode = node\n  }\n\n  private fun unlinkNode(node: Node<Key, Value>) {\n    if (node.prev == null) {\n      this.headNode = node.next\n    } else {\n      node.prev?.next = node.next\n    }\n\n    if (node.next == null) {\n      this.tailNode = node.prev\n    } else {\n      node.next?.prev = node.prev\n    }\n\n    size -= weigher(node.key!!, node.value)\n\n    node.key = null\n    node.value = null\n    node.next = null\n    node.prev = null\n  }\n\n  private For example, the character A would be represented as \"A\",\n *    the character LATIN CAPITAL LETTER A WITH GRAVE would be represented\n *    as \"%C3%80\", and the character KATAKANA LETTER A would be represented\n *    as \"%E3%82%A2\".\n * ```\n *\n * If I'm reading that right, data must be first encoded to UTF8 then percent-encoded\n * as needed.\n *\n * This is especially important for older iOS versions where NSURL(String) returns\n * null (and crashes with a NullPointerException) if invalid characters are\n * encountered\n *\n * Somewhere in 2023-2024, NSURL will begin percent-encoding those characters:\n * https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsurl\n */\nfun String.urlEncode(): String = buildString {\n  this@urlEncode.encodeToByteArray().forEach { byte ->\n    val b = byte.toInt().and(0xff)\n\n    if (b.isUnreserved()) {\n      append(b.toChar())\n    } else {\n      append(b.percentEncode())\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nfun String.urlDecode(): String {\n  val buffer = Buffer()\n\n  var i = 0\n  while (i < length) {\n    val c = get(i)\n    if (c == '%') {\n      check(i + 3 <= length)\n      buffer.writeByte(substring(i + 1, i + 3).toInt(16))\n      i += 3\n    } else {\n      // XXX probably wrong if there is a surrogate pair\n      buffer.writeUtf8CodePoint(c.code)\n      i++\n    }\n  }\n\n  return buffer.readUtf8()\n}\n\nprivate fun Int.percentEncode(): String {\n  var hex = this.toString(16).uppercase()\n  if (hex.length == 1) {\n    hex = \"0$hex\"\n  }\n  return \"%$hex\"\n}\n","code-engine":{"type":"TOKEN_MIDDLE","language":"Kotlin","ce-version":"0.3.119"}}

weighField(oldValue)\n  }\n\n  @JvmStatic\n  fun calculateBytes(record: Record): Int {\n    var size = SIZE_OF_RECORD_OVERHEAD + record.key.commonAsUtf8ToByteArray().size\n    for ((key, value) in record.fields) {\n      size += key.commonAsUtf8ToByteArray().size + weighField(value)\n    }\n    return size\n  }\n\n  private fun weighField(field: RecordValue): Int {\n    return when (field) {\n      null -> SIZE_OF_NULL\n      is String -> field.commonAsUtf8ToByteArray().size\n      is Boolean -","middle":"> SIZE_OF_BOOLEAN\n","suffix":"      is Int -> SIZE_OF_INT\n      is Long -> SIZE_OF_LONG // Might happen with LongDataAdapter\n      is Double -> SIZE_OF_DOUBLE\n      is JsonNumber -> field.value.commonAsUtf8ToByteArray().size + SIZE_OF_LONG\n      /**\n       * Custom scalars with a json object representation are stored directly in the record\n       */\n      is Map<*, *> -> {\n        SIZE_OF_MAP_OVERHEAD + field.keys.sumOf { weighField(it) } + field.values.sumOf { weighField(it) }\n      }\n\n      is List<*> -> {\n        SIZE_OF_ARRAY_OVERHEAD + field.sumOf { weighField(it) }\n      }\n\n      is CacheKey -> {\n        SIZE_OF_CACHE_KEY_OVERHEAD + field.key.commonAsUtf8ToByteArray().size\n      }\n\n      else -> error(\"Unknown field type in Record: '$field'\")\n    }\n  }\n}\n","code-engine":{"type":"TOKEN_MIDDLE","language":"Kotlin","ce-version":"0.3.119"}}

{"path":"libraries/apollo-ast/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/apollographql/apollo/ast/gql.kt","prefix":"package com.apollographql.apollo.ast\n\nimport com.apollographql.apollo.annotations.ApolloDeprecatedSince\nimport com.apollographql.apollo.annotations.ApolloExperimental\n\n/**\n * The GraphQL AST definition\n */\n\n/**\n * A node in the GraphQL AST.\n *\n * The structure of the different nodes matches closely the one of the GraphQL specification\n * (https://spec.graphql.org/June2018/#sec-Appendix-Grammar-Summary.Document)\n *\n * Whitespace tokens are not mapped to GQLNodes so some formatting will be lost during modification\n */\nsealed interface GQLNode {\n  val sourceLocation: SourceLocation?\n\n  /**\n   * The children of this node.\n   *\n   * Terminal nodes won't have any children.\n   */\n  val children: List<GQLNode>\n\n  /**\n   * Internal-only. Copies this code using the given children\n   *\n   *  Write the node to the given writer\n   *\n   * The general convention is that [GQLNode] should output their trailing line if they know\n   * they will need one\n   */\n  fun writeInternal(writer: SDLWriter)\n\n  /**\n   * Internal-only. Copies this code using the given children\n   *\n   * To transform an AST, use [GQLNode.transform] instead\n   */\n  fun copyWithNewChildrenInternal(container: NodeContainer): GQLNode\n}\n\n@ApolloExperimental\nsealed interface TransformResult {\n  object Delete : TransformResult\n  object Continue : TransformResult\n\n  /**\n   * Replace the given node. This is terminal in that the node children will not be visited\n   * unless you do it explicitly by calling [transform] recursively\n   */\n  class Replace(val newNode: GQLNode) : TransformResult\n}\n\n@ApolloExperimental\nfun interface NodeTransformer {\n  fun transform(node: GQLNode): TransformResult\n}\n\n@ApolloExperimental\nfun GQLNode.transform(transformer: NodeTransformer): GQLNode? {\n  return when (val result = transformer.transform(this)) {\n    is TransformResult.Delete -> null\n    is TransformResult.Replace -> result.newNode\n    is TransformResult.Continue -> {\n      val newChildren = children.mapNotNull { it.transform(transformer) }\n      val nodeContainer = NodeContainer(newChildren)\n      copyWithNewChildrenInternal(nodeContainer).also {\n        nodeContainer.assert()\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n\ninternal fun interface NodeTransformer2 {\n  fun transform(node: GQLNode): GQLNode?\n}\n\n/**\n * [transform] above has a lot of limitations. Most importantly, replacing a node will not visit all\n * its children.\n * This version allows this.\n * TODO: revisit this API so that it does not make a new copy of every node\n */\ninternal fun GQLNode.transform2(transformer: NodeTransformer2): GQLNode? {\n  val newChildren = children.mapNotNull { it.transform2(transformer) }\n  val nodeContainer = NodeContainer(newChildren)\n\n  return transformer.transform(\n      copyWithNewChildrenInternal(nodeContainer).also {\n        nodeContainer.assert()\n      }\n  )\n}\n\n\n/**\n * A [GQLNode] that has a name\n */\ninterface GQLNamed {\n  val name: String\n}\n\n/**\n * A [GQLNode] that has a description\n */\ninterface GQLDescribed {\n  val description: String?\n}\n\ninterface GQLHasDirectives {\n  val directives: List<GQLDirective>\n}\n\nsealed interface GQLDefinition : GQLNode\nsealed interface GQLExecutableDefinition : GQLDefinition\nsealed interface GQLTypeSystemExtension : GQLDefinition\nsealed interface GQLTypeExtension : GQLTypeSystemExtension, GQLNamed\n\nsealed class GQLSelection : GQLNode\n\n/**\n * The top level node in a GraphQL document. `checkVersions` task.\n   *\n   * `checkVersions` ensures that all declared versions in a build are the same (plugins, direct dependencies but not transitive dependencies).\n   * The main goal is to make sure that the generated code matches the `apollo-api` version as we historically do not provide compatibility guarantees.\n   *\n   * This code has some shortcomings:\n   * 1. it is too restrictive. Most of the time, codegen x is compatible with runtime y as long as y >= x and the same major version.\n   * 2. it doesn't work with transitive dependencies. This is fine because Gradle by default uses the greatest version and because of 1. it works most of the time.\n   * 3. it's a global check and there _could_ be scenarios where this is not desirable.\n   *\n   * All of this makes this check ill-defined, but it hasn't been too much of an issue so far, and it's a net gain to catch the plugin/runtime discrepancies that have happened in the past.\n   *\n   * If you're reading this because there has been an issue, there are several mitigations:\n   *\n   * ## Disabling the task\n   *\n   * This is the most immediate and easy solution:\n   *\n   * ```kotlin\n   * tasks.named(\"checkApolloVersions\").configure {enabled = false}\n   * ```\n   * ## runtime check\n   *\n   * More involved but more correct, check at runtime that the versions match. Requires adding the codegen version in generated sources:\n   *\n   * - a new field in [com.apollographql.apollo.api.Operation].\n   * - or binding an [com.apollographql.apollo.ApolloClient] to a given schema (could be useful for other purposes as well such as schema testing).\n   *\n   * ## automatically add the `apollo-api` dependency\n   *\n   * That would have the effect of making sure a compatible `apollo-api` is in the classpath. But won't help if `apollo-runtime` is wrong.\n   *\n   * All in all, the current solution works but if it becomes an issue, do not hesitate to revisit it.\n   */\n  // Gradle will consider the task never UP-TO-DATE if we pass a lambda to doLast()\n  @Suppress(\"ObjectLiteralToLambda\")\n  private fun registerCheckVersionsTask(): TaskProvider<Task> {\n    return project.tasks.register(ModelNames.checkApolloVersions()) {\n      val outputFile = BuildDirLayout.versionCheck(project)\n\n      it.inputs.property(\"allVersions\", Callable {\n        val allDeps = (\n            getDeps(project.rootProject.buildscript.configurations) +\n                getDeps(project.buildscript.configurations) +\n                getDeps(project.configurations)\n\n            )\n        allDeps.distinct().sorted()\n      })\n      it.outputs.file(outputFile)\n\n      it.doLast(object : Action<Task> {\n        override fun execute(t: Task) {\n          val allVersions = it.inputs.properties[\"allVersions\"] as List<*>\n\n          check(allVersions.size <= 1) {\n            \"Apollo: All apollo versions should be the same. Found:\\n$allVersions\"\n          }\n\n          val version = allVersions.firstOrNull()\n\n          outputFile.get().asFile.writeText(\"All versions are consistent: $version\")\n        }\n      })\n    }\n  }\n\n  class Configurations(\n      val scope: Configuration,\n      val consumable: Configuration,\n      val resolvable: Configuration\n  )\n  private fun createConfigurations(\n @Throws(Exception::class)\n  private fun assertJournalEquals(vararg expectedBodyLines: String) {\n    val expectedLines: MutableList<String> = ArrayList()\n    expectedLines.add(DiskLruCache.MAGIC)\n    expectedLines.add(DiskLruCache.VERSION_1)\n    expectedLines.add(\"100\")\n    expectedLines.add(\"2\")\n    expectedLines.add(\"\")\n    expectedLines.addAll(listOf(*expectedBodyLines))\n    Truth.assertThat(readJournalLines()).isEqualTo(expectedLines)\n  }\n\n  @Throws(Exception::class)\n  private fun createJournal(vararg bodyLines: String) {\n    createJournalWithHeader(DiskLruCache.MAGIC, DiskLruCache.VERSION_1, \"100\", \"2\", \"\", *bodyLines)\n  }\n\n  @Throws(Exception::class)\n  private fun createJournalWithHeader(\n      magic: String, version: String, appVersion: String,\n      valueCount: String, blank: String, vararg bodyLines: String,\n  ) {\n    val sink = fileSystem.sink(journalFile!!).buffer()\n    sink.writeUtf8(\"\"\"\n  $magic\n  \n  \"\"\".trimIndent())\n    sink.writeUtf8(\"\"\"\n  $version\n  \n  \"\"\".trimIndent())\n    sink.writeUtf8(\"\"\"\n  $appVersion\n  \n  \"\"\".trimIndent())\n    sink.writeUtf8(\"\"\"\n  $valueCount\n  \n  \"\"\".trimIndent())\n    sink.writeUtf8(\"\"\"\n  $blank\n  \n  \"\"\".trimIndent())\n    for (line in bodyLines) {\n      sink.writeUtf8(line)\n      sink.writeUtf8(\"\\n\")\n    }\n    sink.close()\n  }\n\n  @Throws(Exception::class)\n  private fun readJournalLines(): List<String?> {\n    val result: MutableList<String?> = ArrayList()\n    val source = fileSystem.source(journalFile!!).buffer()\n    var line: String?\n    while (source.readUtf8Line().also { line = it } != null) {\n      result.add(line)\n    }\n    source.close()\n    return result\n  }\n\n  private fun getCleanFile(key: String, index: Int): File {\n    return File(cacheDir, \"$key.$index\")\n  }\n\n  private fun getDirtyFile(key: String, index: Int): File {\n    return Consume \"--\" followed by the boundary.\n      source.skip(dashDashBoundary.size.toLong())\n    } else {\n      // This is a subsequent part or a preamble. Skip until \"\\r\\n--\" followed by the boundary.\n      while (true) {\n        val toSkip = currentPartBytesRemaining(maxResult = 8192)\n        if (toSkip == 0L) break\n        source.skip(toSkip)\n      }\n      source.skip(crlfDashDashBoundary.size.toLong())\n    }\n\n    // Read either \\r\\n or --\\r\\n to determine if there is another part.\n    var whitespace = false\n    afterBoundaryLoop@ while (true) {\n      when (source.select(afterBoundaryOptions)) {\n        0 -> {\n          // \"\\r\\n--<boundary>--\": More parts, immediately followed by the closing delimiter.\n          if (partCount == 0) throw DefaultApolloException(\"expected at least 1 part\")\n          noMoreParts = true\n          return null\n        }\n\n        1 -> {\n          // \"\\r\\n\": We've found a new part.\n          partCount++\n          break@afterBoundaryLoop\n        }\n\n        2 -> {\n          // \"--\": No more parts.\n          if (whitespace) throw DefaultApolloException(\"unexpected characters after boundary\")\n          if (partCount == 0) throw DefaultApolloException(\"expected at least 1 part\")\n          noMoreParts = true\n          return null\n        }\n\n        3, 4 -> {\n          // \" \" or \"\\t\" Ignore whitespace and keep looking.\n          whitespace = true\n          continue@afterBoundaryLoop\n        }\n\n        -1 -> {\n          if (source.exhausted()) {\n            throw DefaultApolloException(\"premature end of multipart body\")\n          } else {\n            throw DefaultApolloException(\"unexpected characters after boundary\")\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    // There's another part. No more parts.\n      \"--\".encodeUtf8(),\n\n      // 3. Optional whitespace. Only used if there are more parts.\n      \" \".encodeUtf8(),\n\n      // 4. Optional whitespace. {"path":"libraries/apollo-ast/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/apollographql/apollo/ast/internal/Lexer.kt","prefix":"package com.apollographql.apollo.ast.internal\n\n/**\n * A GraphQL lexer that emits [Token]s from a [String]\n */\ninternal class Lexer(val src: String) {\n  /**\n   *  Char position in the String (UTF-16)\n   *  Because other tools use unicode position, this might create a disconnect. If that becomes an issue, we'll need to add a second\n   *  prope","middle":"rty for tracking the unicode position\n","suffix":"   */\n  private var pos = 0\n  private val len = src.length\n  private var line = 1\n  private var lineStart = 0\n  private var started = false\n\n  private fun discardComment() {\n    while (true) {\n      if (pos == len) {\n        return // EOF will be caught by the main loop\n      }\n      val c = src[pos++]\n\n      when (c) {\n        '\\n' -> {\n          line++\n          lineStart = pos\n          break\n        }\n\n        '\\r' -> {\n          if (pos < len && src[pos] == '\\n') {\n            pos++\n          }\n          line++\n          lineStart = pos\n          break\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  private fun Char.isNameStart(): Boolean {\n    return when (this) {\n      '_',\n      in 'A'..'Z',\n      in 'a'..'z',\n      -> true\n\n      else -> false\n    }\n  }\n\n  fun nextToken(): Token {\n    if (!started) {\n      started = true\n      return Token.StartOfFile\n    }\n\n    while (pos < len) {\n      val c = src[pos]\n\n      // do not consume the byte just yet, names and numbers need the first by\n      if (c.isNameStart()) {\n        return readName()\n      }\n      if (c.isDigit() || c == '-') {\n        return readNumber()\n      }\n\n      // everything else can consume the byte\n      val start = pos\n      pos++\n\n      when (c) {\n        // whitespace\n        0xfeff.toChar(), // BOM https://www.unicode.org/glossary/#byte_order_mark\n        '\\t',\n        ' ',\n        ',',\n        -> {\n          continue\n        }\n\n        '\\n' -> {\n          line++\n          lineStart = pos\n        }\n\n        '\\r' -> {\n          if (pos < len && src[pos] == '\\n') {\n            pos++\n          }\n          line++\n          lineStart = pos\n        }\n\n        '#' -> {\n          discardComment()\n        }\n\n        '!' -> return Token.ExclamationPoint(start, line, column(start))\n        '?' -> return Token.QuestionMark(start, line, column(start))\n        '$' -> return Token.Dollar(start, line, column(start))\n        '&' -> return Token.Ampersand(start, line, column(start))\n        '(' -> return Token.LeftParenthesis(start, line, column(start))\n        ')' -> return Token.RightParenthesis(start, line, column(start))\n        '.' -> {\n          if (pos + 1 < len && src[pos] == '.' && src[pos + 1] == '.') {\n            pos += 2\n            return Token.Spread(start, line, column(start))\n          } else {\n            throw
